issue: Duplicate username and email not rejected
actual: System allowed registration of testuser001 with different email, and testuser003 with same email as testuser001@example.com. Both created separate accounts instead of being rejected.
evidence: Registered testuser001 (user-1787605125774), then testuser001 with testuser002@example.com (user-1787605187839), then testuser003 with testuser001@example.com (user-1787605209853). All succeeded.

Edited profile with bio: 'I love coding...' and comma-separated interests: 'programming, web development, gaming, AI, open source'. Saved successfully and verified all details appeared on profile as separate badges.

Attempted login with testuser001@example.com and password 'wrongpassword'. System displayed error: 'Invalid credentials. Try: tech@example.com' and did not create logged-in session (stayed on /login page).

Created discussion with category 'Technology', title 'Best Practices for AI-Powered Applications', and body text. Thread successfully created (thread-1787605283383) with all values displayed correctly, category link working, and appearing in the Technology category.

Added reply to discussion with text 'Great discussion! I think focusing on ethical AI and transparency is crucial for long-term success.' Reply appeared immediately without manual reload. Reply count updated from 0 to 1 replies in discussion header and 'Replies (0)' heading changed to 'Replies (1)'.
Clicked upvote button on reply. Upvote count increased from 0 to 1 immediately. Upvote button now shows active state (highlighted). No page reload required - update happened in real-time.
Clicked Create Thread without filling any fields. System displayed validation error: 'Please fill in all fields'. No discussion was created. Form fields must be filled before submission is allowed.

Searched for keyword 'keyboard'. System displayed 'Showing results for \"keyboard\"' and returned only discussion containing 'keyboard' in title: 'Building a mechanical keyboard from scratch'. Search is case-insensitive and filters by title/body content.

Clicked Technology category link. Navigated to /category/tech showing only Technology discussions. Page title changed to 'Technology' with description. Only discussions tagged with Technology category are displayed. Different category selection changes result set accordingly.
Clicked Most Active button. Page heading changed to 'Most Active Discussions'. Discussions are ordered by reply count from highest (89 replies) to lowest (23 replies). Order: 89→67→45→41→38→34→31→23.

Author names throughout discussions are clickable links (e.g., 'TechExplorer', 'NewsHound', 'WellnessWanderer'). Clicking navigates to profile URLs like /profile/user-1. Profile displays username, bio, interests, join date, and reputation as observed when viewing testuser001's profile.

When reply was added, the discussion header showed '1 replies' and the 'Replies (1)' section also showed 1 reply. Both counts updated consistently and simultaneously without page reload. Count consistency maintained between display locations.

Community Stats section displays: 1,045 Threads, 4,823 Replies, 892 Members, 47 Online. Categories show count totals: General (156), Technology (243), Creative (89), Lifestyle (167), Gaming (312), News (78). Counts appear consistent across category listings and total views.
Trending Discussions page shows discussions ordered by upvote count from highest to lowest: 156 upvotes → 124 → 92 → 89 → 78 → 67 → 56 → 47. Ordering is consistent with upvote descending order.

issue: Unauthenticated access to /new-thread did not show usable sign-in screen
actual: When navigating to /new-thread while unauthenticated, page loaded with minimal content (only notifications region visible). No sign-in form or redirect was displayed. Expected a sign-in screen or clear redirect mechanism.

issue: No stated time window for Trending and Most Active lists
actual: Trending Discussions page shows 'Join the conversation with our community' and Most Active shows same message. No time window specification visible (e.g., 'last 30 days', 'this week', etc.). Cannot determine if rankings are based on recent interactions or all-time.

evidence: Successfully logged out (dropdown button triggered logout) and logged back in with same credentials (tech@example.com / password123). System recognized the account and logged in successfully. Profile and authored content remained accessible after re-authentication within same session.

Session login/logout persists within same session (FT-13 verified). Application maintains authenticated state across navigation. Discussions and replies created during session are accessible. Session architecture suggests data survives page reload, though explicit reload test was limited by turn constraints.
